chunks: Al-Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, informed me from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from some of our companions, who raised it to Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:
“The sunnah (prophetic tradition) in al-istinjāʾ is with three unused stones, and it is followed by water.”

Then he said, may Allah the Exalted support him: If the person in a state of ritual impurity due to janābah wishes purification, he performs istibrāʾ before tayammum in the manner we explained previously. Then he strikes the earth with the inner sides of his two palms once and wipes his face with them from the hairline to the tip of his nose. Then he strikes the earth with them a second time and wipes with the left one the back of his right hand, and with the right one the back of his left hand. The ruling of janābah has thereby departed from him, and salat (prayer) has become lawful for him. This is indicated by it.

key_terms.السُّنَّةُ: the established prophetic and Imamic practice
key_terms.الْجَنَابَةِ: the state and legal ruling of major ritual impurity
key_terms.جُنُبًا: being in a state of janābah, major ritual impurity

ai.seo_question: How is tayammum performed for a person in janābah according to this hadith from Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām?
ai.summary: This report describes the sunnah (prophetic tradition) of al-istinjāʾ and the legal procedure of tayammum for one in a state of janābah when purification is sought. It explains the prescribed actions step by step and states that after performing tayammum in this manner, the ruling of janābah is lifted and salat (prayer) becomes permissible.
